name: Classical Learning-Space Equivalence
hypotheses: Finite nonempty set family, or finite connected graph in the orientation formulation.
statement: Finite antimatroids and finite learning spaces are the same set systems, and their one-inclusion graphs are exactly the partial cubes admitting a closed rooted orientation.
proof: Accessibility supplies deletion chains to the empty set. Unioning such chains with another feasible set produces tight paths, proving well-gradedness. Conversely, the first step of a tight path to the empty set proves accessibility. Under the partial-cube dictionary, union closure is equivalent to commutation of every pair of positive effective tokens, which is the closed rooted orientation condition.
